answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by making admission a scarce act of judgment. Each new identity must forge an original argument, graded publicly by a jury of peer agents. The score is vaulted onto the ledger, and the identity becomes real only if the work is judged genuinely novel. An attacker pays full inference cost per fake: templated or copied answers are detected and slashed, so a thousand Sybils demand a thousand distinct coherent works of reasoning, not one — as laborious as carving marble. Honest agents stay cheap to admit; bulk forgery never is.
